board.canonical_name: Safe, Auditable Agent Execution in Martech Systems
Provable Downstream Consent, Deletion and Purpose Enforcement
Governance and Review of Generative Marketing Content at Volume
Governed Semantic Context Layer for Agents and Activation
Machine-Readable Commerce Layer and Agent Protocol Interoperability

proposals.name: Measuring presence inside AI answer surfaces
proposals.definition: Brands cannot reliably observe, attribute, or influence how they are represented in LLM assistants and AI search surfaces (ChatGPT, Gemini/AI Mode, Perplexity, Copilot, and in-app assistants), where an increasing share of consideration now happens without a click.
proposals.why_unsolved: The blocker is data access, not analytics maturity. Assistant providers expose no impression, citation, or share-of-voice logs; referral traffic arrives stripped of query context and is a tiny, biased sample of actual exposure; and answers are non-deterministic and personalized, so third-party 'rank trackers' are sampling a distribution they cannot characterize. There is no equivalent of Search Console, no agreed denominator, and no supply-side incentive to create one while the surfaces are pre-monetization. Interventions (llms.txt, schema, PR seeding) have no closed feedback loop to validate.
proposals.evidence: Every GEO/AEO vendor that emerged in 2024-2026 sells synthetic prompt-panel sampling rather than provider-reported data, which is the tell that first-party telemetry does not exist. Meanwhile publishers report double-digit organic declines attributed to AI Overviews/AI Mode, and analytics vendors have had to add 'AI referrer' buckets that capture only the click-through residue of a much larger, invisible impression volume.

proposals.name: No ground truth for incrementality at working budget levels
proposals.definition: After the collapse of deterministic multi-touch attribution, teams have standardized on MMM plus experiments, but cannot validate MMM outputs cheaply or often enough for the models to actually govern budget decisions.
proposals.why_unsolved: Bayesian MMM (Meridian, Robyn, and commercial equivalents) is only as good as its calibration priors, and those priors require geo-holdout or ghost-ad experiments that most advertisers lack the spend, geographic footprint, or platform cooperation to run at per-channel granularity. Platform-native lift tests are graded by the platform being tested and use non-comparable methodologies. Results are unstable across reasonable specification choices, so two competent analysts produce materially different ROAS for the same channel and nothing in the tooling adjudicates between them. Small-and-mid budgets are structurally excluded: the experiment needed to resolve the question costs more than the channel.
proposals.evidence: The tell is behavioral: finance teams increasingly refuse to act on MMM outputs without a matched experiment, and the fastest-growing measurement category is experimentation infrastructure rather than modeling. Open-source MMM adoption spiked but practitioner discourse has shifted from 'which model' to 'how do I know it is right,' which is the calibration gap surfacing.

proposals.name: Consent that does not survive contact with the downstream stack
proposals.definition: Organizations capture consent and preference signals correctly at the edge but cannot demonstrate that those signals are enforced across every downstream destination, warehouse table, model training set, and partner feed.
proposals.why_unsolved: Consent is captured as an event; enforcement requires it to be a persistent, row-level attribute that travels through ETL, joins, aggregations, activation, and vendor SDKs. No standard exists for propagating purpose limitation past the CMP boundary; TCF is ad-tech-specific and not used in US contexts, GPP is partial, and reverse-ETL and CDP destinations generally accept a suppression list rather than a purpose grammar. The practical result is that nobody can produce an audit trail proving a given profile's data was excluded from a given use. The US state patchwork plus universal opt-out mandates makes the required logic per-state and time-varying, and ML training pipelines rarely honor deletion at all.
proposals.evidence: The live driver is litigation rather than regulators: the CIPA/wiretapping and pen-register claim wave over pixels, session replay and chat widgets has continued to expand, and health-adjacent statutes create per-record statutory damages. Companies are settling cases they believed their CMP prevented, which is direct evidence the enforcement layer, not the capture layer, is broken.

proposals.name: Agents as customers break the entire funnel stack
proposals.definition: When an AI agent browses, researches, and transacts on a consumer's behalf, existing web infrastructure cannot distinguish it from abuse, cannot authenticate its principal, cannot personalize for it, and cannot measure it.
proposals.why_unsolved: Three unresolved layers stack. Identity: no widely adopted way for an agent to present verifiable delegated authority, so bot management either blocks legitimate agents or opens a fraud hole. Commerce: agentic checkout protocols emerged fast but merchant-side support for delegated payment credentials, returns liability, and dispute attribution is uneven, and each ecosystem has its own. Measurement and merchandising: analytics attribute agent sessions to bot filters or to nothing, and every persuasion asset a brand owns (imagery, layout, urgency, loyalty framing) is inert against a model that reads structured data. Nobody knows what 'optimizing for the agent' even means as an evaluable objective.
proposals.evidence: Agentic checkout protocols shipped from multiple ecosystems in late 2025 into 2026 with real merchant integrations, so this stopped being hypothetical. In parallel, CDN and bot-management vendors have had to ship 'verified agent' allowlists precisely because their default posture was blocking paying customers, which is a live operational failure rather than a forecast.

proposals.name: Retail and commerce media remain unauditable at scale
proposals.definition: With hundreds of retail, travel, financial and marketplace media networks now selling ads, buyers still cannot compare networks to each other or verify that reported sales lift is incremental.
proposals.why_unsolved: Structurally, the network sells the media, defines the attribution window, matches the transaction, and grades the result, with no log-level export and no independent verification of the closed-loop join. Clean-room access is offered but with query restrictions and aggregation thresholds that specifically prevent reconstructing incrementality. IAB and MRC standards exist on paper; adoption is voluntary and the largest networks have the least incentive to comply because their reported ROAS advantage depends on the current counting rules. Trade dollars blurring with media dollars means the buyer often is not free to walk away, which removes the market pressure that would otherwise force transparency.
proposals.evidence: The persistence of 30-day view-through windows on shopper media, and the routine finding that geo-holdout tests return a fraction of network-reported ROAS, is now common enough to be discussed openly by large advertisers. Consolidation of RMN ad serving into a few tech providers has not produced comparability, which suggests the barrier is commercial, not technical.

proposals.name: No scalable quality gate for machine-generated marketing output
proposals.definition: Teams can generate content, variants, and campaign assets far faster than they can verify them for factual accuracy, legal claim substantiation, brand voice, and regulatory compliance, so human review has become the throughput bottleneck and the risk surface.
proposals.why_unsolved: Evaluation is the missing tool category. Brand and legal compliance are not benchmarkable the way code or math are: the rubric is tacit, org-specific, and changes by jurisdiction and product. LLM-as-judge inherits the generator's blind spots, especially on claim substantiation where the failure mode is a plausible unsupported statement. There is no reliable per-asset provenance either, since C2PA coverage is thin and stripped by most CMS and ad pipelines. So the only working control is sampling review, which does not scale with volume and produces no defensible audit record in regulated categories.
proposals.evidence: The live signal is the reversal pattern: multiple large brands and publishers have pulled AI-generated campaigns or programmatic content after post-publication errors, and regulated verticals have quietly reinstated mandatory human sign-off, which is an admission that automated gating did not work. Ad platforms shipping generative creative tools without corresponding claim-verification tooling widened the gap.

proposals.name: Identity match rates are decaying faster than the replacements mature
proposals.definition: The practical ability to join a customer across owned channels, media platforms, and partner datasets is degrading, and clean rooms and hashed-email graphs do not restore it.
proposals.why_unsolved: The remaining durable key is authenticated email or phone, and its coverage is capped by how many customers log in, which most categories cannot move. Alternative IDs are fragmented with no consolidation in sight and low scale on the browsers that matter. Clean rooms preserve privacy by refusing exactly the row-level joins that would fix match rates, and differential-privacy noise and aggregation floors make small-audience work unreliable. On top of this, IP-based fallbacks are being removed by browser and OS network privacy features, and mobile identifiers keep eroding. The result is that the same customer is counted as several people, silently inflating reach and deflating frequency control, and no tool reports the error bar on the match.
proposals.evidence: Buyers now routinely see reported match rates from platform onboarding that are materially below what the same file achieved two years earlier, and frequency-capping failures in CTV are a recurring, quantified complaint. The fact that third-party cookies were not actually deprecated in Chrome and identity still got worse indicates the cause is the broader privacy stack, not one deprecation event.

proposals.name: Marketing data has no semantics that an agent can be trusted to use
proposals.definition: As teams point LLM agents at warehouses, CDPs, and BI tools to answer questions and take actions, the agents produce confident answers that are wrong because the underlying metric definitions, joins, and filters are ambiguous or contested.
proposals.why_unsolved: The organizational precondition, a single governed semantic layer with agreed definitions of things like an active customer, a qualified lead, or attributed revenue, does not exist in most companies and is a political artifact as much as a technical one. Agent connection protocols made access trivial in 2025-2026 while doing nothing to supply meaning, so the failure mode moved from 'analyst is a bottleneck' to 'wrong number ships at machine speed with no reviewer.' There is also no accepted evaluation harness for analytical agents and no accountability model for who owns an agent-initiated budget or audience change, so governance defaults to either blanket prohibition or unmonitored use.
proposals.evidence: The rapid proliferation of MCP-style connectors into martech and warehouse tools during 2025-2026 happened well ahead of any corresponding semantic-layer or eval tooling, and the recurring enterprise pattern is a pilot that works in demo and is quietly restricted to read-only sandboxes after it contradicts the finance team's numbers.

proposals.name: Measuring AI-mediated discovery
proposals.definition: Marketers cannot produce a defensible, repeatable measure of how often and how their brand appears inside ChatGPT, Gemini/AI Mode, Perplexity and Copilot answers, nor tie that appearance to demand. Current "AI visibility" scores are sampled point estimates presented as facts.
proposals.why_unsolved: The underlying system is stochastic and personalized: repeated runs of the same prompt return different brands and sources, so any score depends on the vendor's prompt set, run count, engine weighting and sampling day. There is no log-file-equivalent ground truth (no impression data from the model providers), so all tooling is synthetic polling without disclosed confidence intervals, and vendors compete on proprietary composites that only their own methodology can move.
proposals.evidence: Multiple 2026 analyses converge on instability rather than tooling immaturity: Brand24's May 2026 practitioner report found the dominant complaint is that AI visibility tools are unreliable or misleading (practitioners calling scores "lottery tickets"), ZeroClick Labs summarized three independent 2026 studies concluding a single reading is mostly noise, and an August 2026 Forbes piece argues the numbers are unreliable but must be measured anyway. That is a measurement-validity argument happening now, two years after GEO tools launched.

proposals.name: The pre-site dark funnel
proposals.definition: A growing share of consideration — shortlisting, comparison, spec checks — happens inside an assistant before any visit, so the first event a brand can observe is a late-funnel session with no upstream context. Budget decisions still have to be made on the observable part.
proposals.why_unsolved: Zero-click means there is no referrer, no query, and often no session at all for the influencing exposure; assistants strip or normalize referral data and a large share of AI-originated sessions land as direct traffic. Neither MTA (nothing to touch) nor MMM (spend on "being cited" is not a spend line) has an input for it, and incrementality testing requires a controllable dial that brands do not have over model retrieval.
proposals.evidence: SparkToro/Similarweb data reported in June 2026 put Google zero-click at ~68%, with Pew showing 8% click-through when an AI Overview is present versus 15% without; Google said at I/O 2026 that AI Mode passed a billion monthly users with query volume more than doubling quarterly. Commerce-side estimates in 2026 claim ~70% of AI referrals are invisible in GA4 and AI contribution is undercounted several-fold. The gap is widening, not stable.

proposals.name: Agent traffic is unclassifiable
proposals.definition: Bots and agents now constitute the majority of web traffic, and marketing systems cannot distinguish a training crawler from a real-time retrieval fetch from a user-directed agent acting on behalf of a buyer — three things with opposite commercial value that all appear as non-human traffic.
proposals.why_unsolved: User-agent strings and IP ranges are voluntary, spoofable and inconsistently declared; mixed-use crawlers deliberately blur search and AI purposes; analytics tools bucket everything non-human into one filtered pile, and personalization, ad serving, consent logic and conversion tracking all silently misbehave when the visitor is an agent. Cryptographic agent attestation standards exist but are not universally adopted, so blocking is a blunt yes/no that risks blocking demand.
proposals.evidence: Cloudflare's CEO stated in June 2026 that bot traffic passed human traffic; Cloudflare's May 2026 data split crawler intent (~52% training, ~9% search); HUMAN's 2026 benchmark reports AI-driven traffic growth of 187% with OpenAI agents ~69% of observed volume; Google only added a distinguishable Google-Agent user agent in March 2026; and Cloudflare's September 15, 2026 default block on mixed-use crawlers on ad pages forces every publisher and brand to make a classification decision they lack data for.

proposals.name: No control loop over how models describe you
proposals.definition: Brands cannot reliably correct false, stale or omitted claims that assistants state about their products, pricing and policies, and cannot verify a fix across models.
proposals.why_unsolved: There is no vendor-side correction channel with an SLA; the only levers are indirect (entity signals, third-party sources, structured data) with unknown latency and no guarantee of propagation. Errors are model-specific and retrieval-specific, so a fix verified in one engine says nothing about another, and failures are dominated by omission and unsupported inference rather than fabrication, which content edits cannot fully prevent.
proposals.evidence: A 2026 study of Google AI Overviews found roughly 11% of atomic claims unsupported by the cited pages, with omission the dominant failure mode; enterprise SEO vendors shipped dedicated "AI accuracy" monitoring products in spring 2026, which indicates detection is now productized while remediation is not. Agentic commerce raises the stakes because misstated shipping or spec data causes an agent to silently drop the offer.

proposals.name: Shipping marketing agents you can trust in production
proposals.definition: Teams can build agents that draft, segment, send and bid, but cannot establish the evaluation, guardrail and rollback infrastructure needed to let them act on customers unsupervised at scale.
proposals.why_unsolved: Marketing outputs are open-ended, so there is no regression test suite equivalent: correctness is contextual, brand-voice and compliance violations are not deterministically detectable, and failures surface as customer harm after the fact. Observability tooling is built for API traces, not for "did this agent make a promise we cannot honor." Adding human approval gates removes the throughput that justified the agent.
proposals.evidence: Sinch's 2026 "AI Production Paradox" research reports 74% of enterprises have already rolled back a deployed AI agent due to governance failures — a retrospective failure statistic, not a forecast — and Gartner-sourced 2026 reporting attributes agent project cancellations to unclear value and inadequate risk controls. Agent fleet sizes are reportedly doubling quarterly while incident detection is deteriorating.

proposals.name: Enforcing consent downstream, not just capturing it
proposals.definition: Capturing a valid opt-out is largely solved; propagating and enforcing it across every destination — ad platforms, CDP, warehouse, email tool, model training corpora, agent context — with an audit trail is not.
proposals.why_unsolved: Consent state lives in a CMP while enforcement must happen in dozens of systems with incompatible suppression semantics and no shared machine-readable preference contract; server-side tagging and conversions APIs bypass the browser layer where the signal was collected. Honoring Global Privacy Control requires acting on a signal that arrives before identity is known, and per-state rule divergence means the enforcement logic is conditional on geolocation that is itself increasingly unreliable.
proposals.evidence: By 2026 roughly twenty US states have enforceable comprehensive privacy laws (Indiana, Kentucky, Rhode Island effective January 1, 2026) and a dozen-plus mandate GPC recognition, with new California audit and risk-assessment obligations. LeanData's 2026 state-of-martech research found fewer than one in three organizations have enforcement mechanisms for the data rules they agree with — capture versus enforcement is the live gap.

proposals.name: Auditing black-box automated buying
proposals.definition: Most paid spend now flows through goal-based automation (Performance Max, AI Max, Advantage+) where the advertiser cannot verify incrementality, separate brand from prospecting demand, or diagnose why performance moved.
proposals.why_unsolved: Platforms optimize toward the conversion signal the advertiser supplies and report on their own attribution, so the system grades its own homework; newly released channel and asset reports are descriptive, not actionable levers. Independent verification requires holdouts the platforms make hard to run cleanly at the geography and duration a mid-size budget can afford, and the automation reallocates during the test.
proposals.evidence: Google shipped meaningful PMax transparency in April 2026 (channel timeline, final URL report, asset-level actuals, larger negative lists) and practitioner analysis immediately concluded the data still cannot be acted on; AI Max reviews through 2026 cite black-box decisions, aggressive query expansion and campaign-level-only negatives. The transparency-without-control pattern is the current complaint, distinct from the older "platforms are opaque" grievance.

proposals.name: No machine-readable layer for agent-mediated commerce
proposals.definition: Brands have no canonical, real-time, structured representation of catalog, price, availability, delivery and policy that agents can consume — and no way to receive customer or performance data back when a transaction is agent-brokered.
proposals.why_unsolved: Product truth is scattered across PIM, ERP, CMS and storefront with conflicting values, and the emerging protocol layer is fragmented across competing specs (ACP, UCP, AP2, card-network agent schemes) with no settled analytics or identity semantics, so merchants integrate multiple times and still receive thin, non-joinable order context. The commercial terms of the data exchange are also unsettled, as the crawler-payment fights show.
proposals.evidence: OpenAI retired Instant Checkout in March 2026 and moved checkout back to merchant environments, resetting integrations after roughly six months; Shopify's Winter '26 agentic storefronts and at least five competing protocols arrived in the same window; 2026 merchant analyses report high agent-referred intent alongside far worse realized conversion, which is an interface and data-readiness failure rather than a demand failure.

proposals.name: Cross-channel causal measurement under privacy and platform fragmentation
proposals.definition: Marketers still cannot reliably determine the incremental effect of spend across walled gardens, connected TV, retail media, search, social, and owned channels. Attribution systems can allocate credit, but they do not consistently establish what would have happened without the exposure.
proposals.why_unsolved: Platforms withhold user-level exposure and auction data; privacy rules prevent durable cross-platform identifiers; conversion APIs use incompatible definitions; and clean rooms cannot create missing counterfactuals. Experiments remain limited by contamination, low statistical power, platform-controlled methodology, and poor coordination across channels.
proposals.evidence: This is likely to remain acute through 2026 because signal loss, modeled platform reporting, retail-media growth, and the shift toward privacy-preserving data sharing all reduce independent observability faster than experimentation infrastructure is improving. August 2026 is beyond my verified knowledge horizon, so this is a forecast from established trends rather than a contemporaneous observation.

proposals.name: Measuring and influencing discovery inside AI answer engines
proposals.definition: Brands cannot reliably measure how often, why, or in what context they appear in generative answers, nor connect those appearances to downstream demand. They also lack a reproducible method for improving inclusion without degrading content for people or traditional search.
proposals.why_unsolved: Answer engines expose little or no impression, prompt, citation, audience, or conversion data; responses vary by model, retrieval corpus, personalization, and time; and automated monitoring uses synthetic prompts that may not represent actual users. Referral traffic captures only the small fraction of answer-engine influence that produces a click.
proposals.evidence: AI-mediated discovery is expanding while traffic and measurement interfaces remain much thinner than those available for search advertising or SEO. Rapid model and retrieval changes also make yesterday's visibility tests difficult to reproduce.

proposals.name: Reliable identity and consent propagation across the customer journey
proposals.definition: Even well-funded organizations cannot maintain a complete, accurate, permission-aware customer identity across browsers, apps, devices, stores, call centers, partners, and advertising platforms. The result is both missed recognition and inappropriate activation.
proposals.why_unsolved: Deterministic identifiers cover only part of the journey; probabilistic matching is uncertain; platforms do not reveal their identity graphs; household and individual identities are easily conflated; and consent purposes, jurisdictions, revocations, and retention rules do not map consistently between systems. A CDP can centralize records but cannot recover absent signals or prove every downstream system honored a change.
proposals.evidence: Server-side collection, clean rooms, first-party identifiers, and CDPs have proliferated precisely because browser and mobile identifiers became less dependable, yet none supplies universal, permission-correct recognition. Regulatory divergence makes propagation harder rather than merely unfinished.

proposals.name: Production-safe autonomous marketing agents
proposals.definition: Marketing agents cannot yet be trusted to plan and execute consequential campaigns across ad platforms, CRM, commerce, and content systems with bounded cost, policy compliance, and predictable outcomes. Human review still becomes the real control plane for many high-impact actions.
proposals.why_unsolved: Models are nondeterministic and susceptible to prompt injection; martech APIs have inconsistent semantics and permissions; agents lack robust transaction rollback and shared state; and there are no mature evaluations that cover long-running, cross-system business workflows. Audit logs often show tool calls without adequately explaining intent or validating business consequences.
proposals.evidence: Vendors are moving from copilots that draft material to agents that alter budgets, audiences, journeys, and assets. That transition makes reliability, authorization, observability, and rollback immediate deployment blockers rather than hypothetical AI-safety concerns.

proposals.name: A trustworthy semantic and data-quality layer for AI-driven marketing
proposals.definition: Teams cannot reliably give analytics tools and AI agents a shared, current understanding of metrics, customers, products, campaigns, and business rules. Plausible outputs frequently conceal inconsistent definitions or broken source data.
proposals.why_unsolved: Warehouses contain duplicated and drifting schemas; event instrumentation changes silently; metric definitions differ by team and platform; lineage becomes incomplete across SaaS tools; and unstructured institutional knowledge is not machine-enforceable. Retrieval and semantic layers can surface documentation, but they do not determine which conflicting definition is correct or detect every behavioral change upstream.
proposals.evidence: Generative analytics and agents have made semantic inconsistency operationally dangerous: incorrect definitions can now trigger actions at scale, not merely produce disputed dashboards. The renewed investment in metric layers, catalogs, and AI observability indicates that existing stacks do not resolve the problem.

proposals.name: Comparable, deduplicated retail-media measurement
proposals.definition: Advertisers cannot consistently compare retail-media networks or determine incremental sales after accounting for organic purchases, trade promotion, other media, and duplicated audiences. Reported return on ad spend remains heavily dependent on each retailer's attribution rules.
proposals.why_unsolved: Retailers use different product taxonomies, attribution windows, identity coverage, and definitions of sales and new customers; transaction data remains inside separate closed environments; and there is no broadly enforced standard for exposure-level deduplication or independent incrementality testing. Clean rooms enable selected joins but do not force comparable methodology or disclose missing data.
proposals.evidence: Retail media is absorbing larger budgets and expanding off-site and into connected TV, increasing overlap with other channels. Standardization efforts themselves are evidence that buyers still lack comparable outputs, while retailer incentives favor proprietary measurement.

proposals.name: Scalable provenance, rights, and brand-safety control for generated content
proposals.definition: Organizations cannot automatically prove that every generated image, video, voice, claim, and adaptation is legally usable, factually supported, on-brand, and properly disclosed in every market and channel. Manual review does not scale to the volume promised by generative production.
proposals.why_unsolved: Model providers generally cannot supply asset-level training provenance; similarity and copyright tests are inconclusive; licensing terms vary across models and jurisdictions; factual and brand checks are context-dependent; and provenance metadata can be stripped during distribution. Detection cannot reliably establish whether an asset was generated or whether it infringes a protected work.
proposals.evidence: Generated content is moving from experimentation into high-volume localization and personalization while litigation, disclosure rules, impersonation risks, and synthetic-media fraud remain unsettled. Increasing output volume widens the gap between production speed and review capacity.

proposals.name: Independent governance of opaque, continuously changing marketing platforms
proposals.definition: Enterprises cannot continuously verify that every model, audience, optimization rule, data transfer, and subprocessor in their martech stack behaves within legal and organizational policy. Point-in-time procurement and compliance reviews become obsolete as cloud platforms and embedded models change.
proposals.why_unsolved: Vendors can modify models and data flows without exposing implementation details; contractual descriptions are coarser than actual processing; nested subprocessors and cross-border transfers are difficult to inventory; and audit tooling rarely connects consent, model versions, prompts, decisions, and downstream actions in one evidentiary chain.
proposals.evidence: AI features are being embedded throughout existing SaaS products rather than purchased only as discrete systems, multiplying unreviewed model and data dependencies. Faster release cycles and expanding AI regulation make periodic questionnaires structurally inadequate.

proposals.name: Decision-grade cross-channel causal measurement
proposals.definition: Marketers still cannot reliably determine the incremental business effect of each channel across search, social, CTV, retail media, creators, gaming and offline activity. Attribution, incrementality tests and marketing-mix models frequently produce conflicting answers.
proposals.why_unsolved: Exposure and outcome data remain trapped in platforms and clean rooms; privacy protections remove person-level signals; channels use inconsistent outcome definitions; and experiments often lack sufficient controls or statistical power. No accepted method currently reconciles these imperfect approaches into one timely, comparable allocation signal.
proposals.evidence: IAB’s 2026 State of Data found that up to 75% of buy-side respondents believe advanced measurement underperforms on rigor, timeliness, trust or efficiency. IAB consequently launched the multi-year Project Eidos around harmonization, cross-channel outcomes, incrementality and modernized MMM. ([iab.com](https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/IAB_StateofDataReport_February_2026pdf.pdf?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Safe governance of autonomous marketing agents
proposals.definition: Organizations cannot yet let agents independently change campaigns, spend money, publish content or interact with customers while reliably keeping behavior within brand, legal, privacy and financial constraints.
proposals.why_unsolved: Agent behavior is nondeterministic and crosses systems with different permissions. Existing controls do not consistently provide task-scoped authorization, pre-action validation, evaluation under realistic conditions, end-to-end audit trails, rollback and clear accountability for delegated or multi-agent actions.
proposals.evidence: Eighty-one percent of martech leaders were already implementing or piloting agents by mid-2025, while 2026 research identifies security, data integrity, compliance, brand consistency and visibility into agent actions as leading concerns. New IAB and NAI controls issued in 2026 show that governance is still being constructed alongside deployment rather than being solved infrastructure. ([gartner.com](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-12-04-cmos-top-challenges-and-priorities-for-2026?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Measurement of AI-mediated discovery and demand
proposals.definition: Brands cannot reliably measure how often AI systems surface, omit or characterize them—or connect an AI-generated recommendation to a later purchase that may occur without a click or observable referral.
proposals.why_unsolved: AI responses vary by model, prompt, location, personalization and time; platforms expose little query-level or downstream behavior; and competing visibility tools use incompatible prompt libraries and scoring methods. Even visibility does not establish persuasion, incrementality or commerce attribution.
proposals.evidence: As of August 3, 2026, IAB reported more than 20 AI-visibility vendors producing potentially different answers for the same brand, with only 16% of brands systematically tracking visibility. Its new framework explicitly leaves paid placement and downstream commerce attribution for future work; Google’s dedicated generative-AI reporting was still rolling out experimentally in June. ([iab.com](https://www.iab.com/guidelines/measuring-visibility-in-the-ai-era/?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Reliable, semantically usable data for AI activation
proposals.definition: Even well-funded teams cannot consistently give models and agents a current, complete and correctly interpreted view of customers, products, content, offers and business rules across the martech stack.
proposals.why_unsolved: The blocker is not simply moving records into a warehouse or CDP. Source systems disagree on identifiers and definitions; metadata and lineage are incomplete; unstructured knowledge is poorly governed; freshness varies; and business semantics are usually encoded in undocumented human workflows. Agents therefore retrieve technically valid but contextually wrong data.
proposals.evidence: IAB identifies fragmented data, inconsistent definitions and unreliable exposure-to-outcome connections as foundational 2026 problems. Gartner says data quality is now a direct driver of AI advertising outcomes, while only 30% of CMOs report mature AI readiness despite allocating 15.3% of marketing budgets to AI. ([iab.com](https://www.iab.com/topics/project-eidos/?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Portable identity, consent and permitted-use enforcement
proposals.definition: The ecosystem cannot reliably preserve who or what may use a customer’s data, for which purpose and under which jurisdiction as data moves among brands, publishers, clouds, clean rooms, activation platforms and AI systems.
proposals.why_unsolved: Identity matching loses coverage across devices and environments, while consent is contextual rather than a permanent attribute. State and international rules diverge, vendor interpretations differ, and privacy-enhancing computation can protect a join without proving that every downstream model use or activation remains authorized.
proposals.evidence: IAB Tech Lab continues expanding jurisdiction-specific consent strings and clean-room interoperability protocols, while acknowledging the need for consensus and additional standards. Meanwhile, W3C’s privacy-preserving attribution API remained a working draft in 2026 with unresolved issues and explicit accuracy-versus-privacy constraints. ([iabtechlab.com](https://iabtechlab.com/gpp/?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Trusted interoperability for agentic advertising and commerce
proposals.definition: Buyer, seller, marketing and consumer agents cannot yet interact across vendors with dependable shared meanings, verified identities, delegated authority and predictable transaction behavior.
proposals.why_unsolved: General agent protocols do not encode advertising taxonomies, campaign constraints, privacy signals or commercial intent. Multiple emerging ad and payment protocols still have to achieve broad adoption, reconcile competing trust registries and represent exactly what a person authorized an agent to do.
proposals.evidence: IAB Tech Lab spent 2026 building AAMP, agent registries and agent-specific advertising schemas because ambiguity between agents can be operationally catastrophic. Visa separately created a cryptographic protocol so merchants can distinguish authorized shopping agents from malicious bots, while Mastercard identifies verifiable intent, identity and permission as unresolved prerequisites for scale. ([iabtechlab.com](https://iabtechlab.com/standards/aamp-agentic-advertising-management-protocols/?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Scalable content quality, provenance and rights control
proposals.definition: Marketing teams cannot generate and personalize content at AI speed while consistently proving source rights, factual accuracy, brand fidelity and appropriate disclosure across every asset and channel.
proposals.why_unsolved: Generation is easier than validation. Provenance metadata can be stripped or lost; rights and likeness permissions are not machine-readable end to end; brand rules contain subjective exceptions; and automated detectors cannot reliably establish whether content is authentic, licensed or misleading.
proposals.evidence: AI copy production reached 91% adoption in one 2026 martech survey, while content-authenticity and AI-detection tooling had the highest non-adoption count. IAB issued its first disclosure framework only in January 2026 amid fragmented regulation and found a 37-point gap between advertiser assumptions and younger consumers’ sentiment toward AI ads. ([content.martechday.com](https://content.martechday.com/state-of-martech-2026.pdf?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Independent control of black-box media optimization
proposals.definition: Marketers cannot independently verify or tightly constrain how platform AI systems choose audiences, inventory, bids, creative combinations and budget shifts—or whether reported gains merely capture demand that would have converted anyway.
proposals.why_unsolved: Platforms hold the richest auction and exposure data, optimize against proprietary proxy objectives and report their own performance. External tools receive delayed, aggregated outputs rather than decision logs or valid counterfactuals, making auditing, cross-platform coordination and long-term-value optimization unreliable.
proposals.evidence: IAB explicitly names platform-embedded optimization as a source of measurement strain, while 66% of surveyed buyers planned increased focus on agentic campaign execution in 2026. The July 2026 AAMP release added pricing integrity and approval thresholds, indicating that independent operational controls are only now being standardized. ([iab.com](https://www.iab.com/insights/2026-state-of-data-report/?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Measurement Fragmentation Across Privacy Sandboxes and Walled Gardens
proposals.definition: Inability to reconcile conversion paths and calculate cross-platform incremental lift across disparate privacy-preserving measurement frameworks (e.g., Apple Private Click Measurement, Android Privacy Sandbox, clean rooms) without deterministic identifiers.
proposals.why_unsolved: Each major ecosystem enforces mutually incompatible aggregation thresholds, noise addition mechanisms (differential privacy), and delayed reporting structures that mathematically preclude unbiasing and unified cross-channel deduplication.
proposals.evidence: The deprecation of third-party cookies alongside distinct, non-interoperable API architectures introduced by major ad platforms has forced reliance on high-latency MMMs that cannot guide real-time tactical bidding.

proposals.name: Autonomous Marketing Agent Execution Safety and Drift
proposals.definition: The risk and lack of deterministic guardrails when deploying autonomous LLM-driven agents to execute programmatic media adjustments, copy generation, and multi-step workflow changes directly into production systems.
proposals.why_unsolved: Agentic loops lack reliable verification layers and stateful rollbacks for multi-system API side effects, leading to hallucinated targeting parameters, budget overrun cascades, or compliance violations before humans can intervene.
proposals.evidence: Widespread enterprise deployment of agentic workflows has resulted in operational teams pulling back automated write-access to core ad and CRM platforms in favor of manual review bottlenecks.

proposals.name: Synthetic Content Authenticity and Brand Governance at Scale
proposals.definition: The challenge of tracking provenance, copyright compliance, model licensing lineage, and brand standard adherence across thousands of dynamically generated creative assets.
proposals.why_unsolved: C2PA metadata and watermarking are easily stripped by intermediary ad networks, social feeds, and compression pipelines, while automated brand QA models cannot consistently detect subtle visual or tonal misalignments before ad delivery.
proposals.evidence: The explosion of generative AI creative engines has overwhelmed traditional creative review teams, yet fully automated QA systems generate high false-positive rates on subjective brand guidelines.

proposals.name: Composable CDP Semantic Drift and Real-Time Activation Latency
proposals.definition: The breakdown of data consistency and activation speed when building customer profiles across decoupled data warehouses, reverse ETL pipelines, and specialized edge tools.
proposals.why_unsolved: Underlying cloud data warehouses optimize for analytical throughput rather than millisecond-level point lookups; meanwhile, decoupled schemas lack a centralized semantic contract, causing logic divergence between analytical and operational systems.
proposals.evidence: Enterprises migrating from packaged CDPs to warehouse-native architectures frequently report data latency of minutes-to-hours for event triggering and conflicting segment counts between BI and downstream execution tools.

proposals.name: Consent Graph Sync Across Fragmented Global Regulatory Frameworks
proposals.definition: The technical inability to propagate complex, jurisdiction-specific consent states and purpose-limitations synchronously across an enterprise's entire distributed tech stack.
proposals.why_unsolved: Consent management platforms (CMPs) capture preferences at the edge, but downstream operational systems, vendor tags, and reverse-ETL flows lack standardized, bidirectional protocol mechanisms to enforce purpose-based access controls dynamically at query time.
proposals.evidence: Increasingly divergence among regional privacy laws (e.g., EU AI Act, US state-level privacy statutes) has led to automated workflows processing restricted data due to asynchronous consent propagation delays.

proposals.name: B2B Multi-Touch Incrementality Under Signal Obfuscation
proposals.definition: Measuring true pipeline incrementality and buying committee influence in B2B environments amid email security scanners, IP masking, and hybridized buying journeys.
proposals.why_unsolved: Aggressive corporate security filters trigger false clicks/opens, while privacy features obscure corporate IP addresses, destroying the fidelity of lead-to-account matching heuristics used by ABM platforms.
proposals.evidence: B2B go-to-market teams are seeing a sharp increase in ghost engagement data and mismatched buying intent signals, forcing a return to subjective pipeline sourcing methodologies.

proposals.name: Deterministic Identity Decay in Ephemeral Browsing Environments
proposals.definition: The continuous erosion of persistent cross-session user identity caused by aggressive browser-level storage partitioning, private relay networks, and dynamic IP cycling.
proposals.why_unsolved: First-party cookies set via JavaScript are capped or partitioned by browser privacy protections, and server-side tagging workarounds are increasingly constrained by network-level proxy anonymization and browser storage caps.
proposals.evidence: Known-to-unknown user ratios in mid-funnel conversion funnels are degrading year-over-year, despite significant investment in server-side tracking infrastructure and first-party identity graphs.

proposals.name: Cross-Walled-Garden Incrementality Reconciliation
proposals.definition: The inability to measure true, net-incremental business lift and eliminate duplicated conversion claims across walled gardens (Meta, Google, Amazon, Retail Media Networks) and offline channels in operational time.
proposals.why_unsolved: Platform-enforced privacy boundaries, differential privacy noise thresholds, and the refusal of dominant ad networks to allow raw user-level joins make deterministic multi-touch attribution technically impossible. Marketers are forced to triangulate between aggregated, slow-moving Marketing Mix Models (MMM) and walled-garden conversion APIs that each claim credit for the same conversions.
proposals.evidence: IAB State of Data reports show over 70% of enterprise marketers report measurement models fail to represent cross-channel reality, while the explosion of Retail Media Networks has fractured conversion data across dozens of isolated, self-attributing silos [1.2.3].

proposals.name: Persistent Identity Unification Under Ephemeral Browser/OS Constraints
proposals.definition: The failure of identity resolution systems to maintain deterministic, cross-device customer profiles across unauthenticated sessions as client-side storage lifetimes are aggressively curtailed.
proposals.why_unsolved: Platform defenses (Safari ITP, Android Privacy Sandbox, Private Relay) actively penalize heuristic fingerprinting and truncate first-party cookie lifespans to 1–7 days. Because unauthenticated traffic represents 80%+ of site visits, first-party identity graphs collapse into fragmented, duplicate 'ghost' profiles without frequent explicit user logins.
proposals.evidence: Despite heavy enterprise investment in Customer Data Platforms (CDPs) and server-side tagging, match rates for mid-funnel unauthenticated traffic remain below 30%, driving high churn in CDP customer satisfaction surveys.

proposals.name: Black-Box AI Agent Collision and Campaign Cannibalization
proposals.definition: The lack of cross-platform orchestration to prevent autonomous optimization engines (e.g., Google Performance Max, Meta Advantage+, autonomous CRM bots) from bidding against each other or over-saturating identical audiences.
proposals.why_unsolved: Each advertising and automation vendor operates proprietary, black-box reinforcement learning models that optimize purely for their own platform's conversions. There is no open, standard cross-agent communication protocol or sub-second governance layer capable of arbitrating competing algorithmic decisions across external systems.
proposals.evidence: The widespread enterprise shift to fully automated campaign types has created documented issues with self-bidding on branded terms, audience fatigue, and margin erosion that performance teams can only detect after ad spend is exhausted.

proposals.name: Data Clean Room Interoperability and Query Fragmentation
proposals.definition: The lack of federated querying and standardized multi-party computation across disparate data clean rooms, forcing brands to build and maintain separate pipelines for each publisher ecosystem.
proposals.why_unsolved: Clean room vendors (Snowflake, AWS, Google Ads Data Hub, Amazon Marketing Cloud) rely on conflicting identity backbones (UID2, RampID, proprietary graph IDs), incompatible SQL dialects, and differing differential privacy loss budgets, deliberately preserving structural vendor lock-in.
proposals.evidence: With major retailers launching independent retail media clean rooms, CPG and retail brands must navigate 10+ incompatible clean room environments, multiplying data engineering overhead without achieving a single unified dataset.

proposals.name: Analytics Contamination from AI Crawlers and Synthetic Agents
proposals.definition: The inability of web and product analytics platforms to isolate non-human traffic generated by agentic AI bots, LLM research crawlers, and autonomous scrapers from real consumer behavioral data.
proposals.why_unsolved: Modern AI agents render JavaScript, mimic human interaction latencies, and execute headless browsing via residential IP pools. Traditional user-agent and IP-based filtering tools cannot distinguish an autonomous buying bot or AI researcher from an authentic user without introducing high-friction CAPTCHAs that damage conversion rates.
proposals.evidence: Telemetry data shows autonomous AI bots and scrapers accounting for up to 30-50% of unauthenticated web traffic, skewing bounce rates, session durations, and top-of-funnel lead scoring models across B2B and B2C stacks.

proposals.name: Composable CDP Latency and Schema Drift in Operational Triggering
proposals.definition: The operational failure of warehouse-native martech architectures to support sub-second, stateful event triggers due to data warehouse sync latencies and frequent data model breaking changes.
proposals.why_unsolved: Cloud data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks) are architected for columnar batch processing rather than low-latency operational key-value lookups. Reverse-ETL sync schedules (5–15+ minute intervals) fail real-time trigger use cases (such as cart abandonment or in-session personalization), while upstream data engineering changes routinely break downstream marketing automation payloads.
proposals.evidence: Enterprise migrations to 'composable CDPs' have frequently stalled or required secondary real-time streaming infrastructure layers because warehouse-native approaches cannot meet sub-second SLA requirements for transactional personalization.

proposals.name: Generative Creative Governance, Hallucination Drift, and Asset Degradation
proposals.definition: The lack of automated, deterministic compliance and quality assurance tools capable of evaluating thousands of dynamic, AI-generated creative and copy variants in real time.
proposals.why_unsolved: Generative models are non-deterministic, making absolute enforcement of strict brand voice, regulatory disclosure rules, and factual accuracy computationally difficult at millisecond generation speeds. Automated LLM-as-a-judge evaluation layers add significant latency and can hallucinate during policy evaluations.
proposals.evidence: Major martech landscape reports highlight significant consolidation and workflow abandonment in generative content tools, as marketing teams hit human-in-the-loop bottlenecks to prevent brand dilution and compliance violations.

proposals.name: Real-Time Consent and Privacy Preference Propagation Across Decentralized Stacks
proposals.definition: The failure to reliably and instantaneously synchronize opt-outs, deletion requests, and dynamic consent states across dozens of loosely coupled downstream SaaS tools and adtech endpoints.
proposals.why_unsolved: Downstream SaaS platforms use inconsistent, asynchronous APIs with no universal consent webhook standard. Local data caches, shadow data pipelines, and third-party sync cadences mean revoked user consent or Global Privacy Control (GPC) signals frequently take hours or days to propagate across all edge destinations.
proposals.evidence: Regulatory enforcement under state privacy frameworks (such as CPRA) has intensified around latent data sharing and pixel fire delays, where brands fail compliance audits despite utilizing enterprise Consent Management Platforms (CMPs).
